Ref: CALEA
Standard 71.1.1-7;
71.2.1; 71.3.1-3;
71.4.1
DEPARTMENTAL
GENERAL
ORDER
O-2
Rev.
23 Mar 00
Index as:
Fugitive Unit Vehicles
Guarding Prisoners
Hospitalization of Adult and
Juvenile Prisoners
Juveniles, Transporting
Prisoners, Transporting and
Guarding
Responsibilities of Transporting
Officers
Transportation of Prisoners and
Persons in Custody
Vehicles for Transportation of
Prisoners
Page 1 o 14
TRANSPORTATION OF PRISONERS AND PERSONS IN CUSTODY
The purpose of this order is to set forth Departmental policy and procedure
regarding the transportation, medical care, and guarding of prisoners and persons
in custody.
I. GENERAL TRANSPORTATION OPERATIONS AND POLICY
A. A patrol wagon shall be the standard method of transporting
prisoners and it shall contain separate compartments for males and
females. Whenever a patrol wagon is used to transport persons in
custody, the driver and the wagon officer shall sit in the front seats
separated from the prisoner(s) by a safety barrier that prevents the
prisoner(s) from having access to the driver’s compartment. Officers
shall use the seat belts when the wagon is in motion. The safety
barrier between the front and rear compartments should not impair
conversation and it should promote the safety of the occupants in the
front and/or rear compartments.
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
B. Patrol wagons shall be used to transport:
1. Adults from the point of custody to the Jail or a hospital.
2. All juveniles 12 years old and older from the point of custody
to the Youth Services Division (YSD), a hospital, or the
Juvenile Probation Department.
3. All juveniles under 12 years of age shall be transported in
standard police cars.
4. The YSD receiving officer shall be consulted before juveniles
are transported in accordance with the provisions of
Departmental General Order O-3, PROCESSING JUVENILE
OFFENDERS.
C. Prisoners shall be handcuffed in accordance with the provisions and
techniques described in Departmental Training Bulletin III-B.4,
HANDCUFFING and Special Order 4725, POSITIONAL
ASPHYXIA (20 Oct 95).
D. Use Of Marked/Caged Vehicles
1. Whenever circumstances necessitate using a standard police
patrol car to transport persons in custody, prior approval from
a supervisory officer shall be required. He/she shall specify
whether a one or two officer unit shall be assigned.
2. If two officers are in the vehicle, both officers shall sit in the
front seat.
E. Use Of Uncaged Vehicles
1. A lone officer shall avoid transporting a prisoner in a vehicle
not equipped with a cage divider. If such transportation is
imperative, the prisoner’s hands shall be handcuffed behind
his/her back and he/she is to be seated in the front passenger
seat of the vehicle with the seat belt fastened.
Page 2 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
2. When two officers are transporting one or two prisoners in a
vehicle not equipped with a cage divider, the second officer
shall sit behind the driver with the prisoner(s) seated to
his/her right, handcuffed and with the seat belt(s) fastened.
Caution shall be taken to keep the second officer’s gun side
away from the prisoner. No more than two prisoners shall be
transported in a vehicle not equipped with a cage divider.
F. The Communications Division shall be responsible for the
assignment of patrol wagons for the transport of persons in custody.
1. At the request of the Jail or YSD, the Communications
Division shall assign a wagon officer(s) to transport a
person(s) in custody from the Jail to the hospital or from YSD
to the hospital or to Juvenile Probation Department facilities,
including the facility at 150th Avenue in San Leandro.
2. Requests for use of patrol wagons beyond the scope of Part I,
F, 1 of this order (e.g., prisoner transport from other
jurisdictions) must be approved in advance by the Patrol
Division watch commander.
G. Whenever a female is transported in a standard police car, male
transporting officers shall inform the Communications Division by
radio at the beginning and at the end of the trip of both their location
and their vehicle's odometer reading.
H. Seat belts or safety restraint devices shall be worn by all occupants
in accordance with the provisions of Departmental General Order
J-4, EMERGENCY DRIVING, PURSUIT (CODE 3), PURSUIT
INTERVENTION & SAFETY BELT REGULATIONS.
I. Under no circumstances shall any vehicle with a prisoner be
involved in a pursuit or any activity that would jeopardize the safety
of the prisoner or enhance his/her chances for escape.
J. In cases where a sick, injured, or disabled prisoner is being
transported, arrangements shall be made to accommodate conditions
Page 3 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
for their transport that dictate special care and attention. The
following are examples to consider:
1. The type of vehicle to be used when transporting non-
ambulatory prisoners or those requiring wheelchairs,
crutches, or prosthetic appliances.
Prisoners in wheelchairs shall be transported directly to Santa
Rita.
2. The transfer of medicine, insulin, and other special items for
sick, injured, or disabled prisoners during transport.
3. The safety of the transporting officer and the sick, injured, or
disabled prisoner.
K. In cases where a prisoner is transported in special situations, such as
attending funerals, visiting critically ill persons, or attending the
reading of a will, arrangements shall be made in accordance with
current Jail procedures. Precautions and security measures shall be
taken in accordance with the provisions of this order.
II. TRANSPORTING OFFICERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The officer in control of the vehicle is responsible for the safety and
custody of any prisoner in his/her vehicle. A transporting officer’s
primary responsibility is the safe delivery of the prisoner(s) in their
care.
B. The transporting officer(s) shall examine the transporting vehicle
before beginning each shift to ensure that the vehicle has not been
tampered with since last used and is free of weapons and/or
evidence.
C. The transporting officer shall search every prisoner before being
transported. The search shall ensure that the prisoner is not in
possession of any weapons and/or evidence.
Page 4 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
D. Whenever the driver backs up, the passenger officer shall get out
and guide him/her.
E. An officer shall not stop to render assistance in unrelated matters.
Except in obvious and extreme circumstances, the officer shall notify
the Communications Division of the location and nature of the
incident. Under no circumstances will a prisoner in a police vehicle
be left unguarded.
F. The prisoner’s right to communicate with others, such as to an
attorney or family member, shall not be exercised during the period
that the prisoner is being transported.
G. Upon arrival at the given destination, the officer(s) transporting
prisoners to a facility must ensure that:
1. All firearms are secured and in safekeeping.
2. Restraining devices are not removed until instructed to do so
by Jail personnel in accordance with current Jail procedures.
3. All documentation regarding the transfer is delivered to the
receiving officer.
4. Prior notification is made to Jail personnel of any potential
medical or security hazards so that necessary preparations can
be made.
5. All necessary signatures from and/or written documentation
detailing the prisoner transaction are obtained from the
receiving officer.
H. Once a prisoner(s) has been transported and removed from the
vehicle, a thorough search of the transporting vehicle shall be
conducted as soon as practical, but, in all cases, before the vehicle is
reused, to ensure that the vehicle has not been tampered with since
last used, is free of weapons and/or evidence, and that all personal
property has been removed and transferred with the prisoner(s).
Page 5 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
I. In the event of an escape, the transporting officer shall immediately:
1. Notify the Communications Division and furnish the
following information:
a. That an escape has occurred
b. Description of escapee
c. Direction of flight
d. Charges
2. Notify and advise the Communications Division via telephone
to broadcast a Communications Order and notify other
agencies, if necessary.
3. Complete a supplemental report if additional charges are
added.
4. Notify a field supervisor who shall make a Patrol Log entry
and notify the Watch Commander.
J. At least one officer shall remain with the vehicle and guard the
prisoners at all times.
III. SEPARATION OF PRISONERS AND PERSONS IN CUSTODY
A. A prisoner whose attitude, condition or conduct is such as to
constitute a threat to the safety of him/herself or other persons inside
the vehicle shall be transported separately in another vehicle or, in
the case of compartmentalized wagons, in a separate section of the
wagon.
B. When being transported in compartmentalized wagons, adult
prisoners ordinarily shall be separated by sex and placed in different
sections of the vehicle. In non-compartmentalized wagons, adults
may be transported together regardless of sex.
Page 6 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
C. Juveniles shall be separated as follows:
1. Juveniles in custody for Welfare and Institutions Code Section
300 (Protective Custody) may be transported together
regardless of sex. They shall not be transported in the same
vehicle or compartment with juvenile offenders or adults.
2. Juveniles in custody for Welfare and Institutions Code
Sections 601 and 602 violations shall not be transported with
adults, nor shall they be transported with prisoners of the
opposite sex except under extraordinary circumstances or with
the permission of a supervisor. Examples of extraordinary
circumstances are as follows:
a. When a compartmentalized vehicle is unavailable and
actual or potential interference from bystanders
requires the quick removal of suspects from the arrest
scene.
b. A riot or other disturbance requires prompt
transportation of large numbers of prisoners whose
ages cannot easily be determined.
c. When extreme emergencies or priorities prevent
dispatching of more than one transporting vehicle.
D. Juvenile Disposition
1. At the request of a YSD receiving officer, the transporting
officer will stand by until a juvenile prisoner is safely
secured. When appropriate, the transporting officer will
deliver the juvenile to the Jail Division for intoxication tests
or female searches.
2. Juveniles arrested or taken into custody must be turned over
to the Juvenile Probation Department within six (6) hours
from the time they enter the police building.
Page 7 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
IV. ILL OR INJURED PERSONS
A. Medical Care and Clearance
1. Adult and juvenile prisoners who need medical care shall be
transported to Highland General Hospital except in
emergency situations, in which case the closest emergency
hospital shall be utilized.
2. The Jail Division and YSD shall not accept arrested persons
for booking without medical clearance if they need medical
treatment or evaluation.
a. Booking personnel shall require medical clearance if
the prisoner is semiconscious, unconscious, incoherent,
unable to stand without assistance, or suffering from a
physical condition that requires a physician' s
evaluation.
b. Disagreements between transportation and booking
personnel regarding the physical condition of adult
prisoners shall be referred to the Jail Division watch
supervisor for final resolution.
c. The YSD commander or supervisor shall resolve
disagreements between transportation and booking
personnel regarding the physical condition of juvenile
prisoners. In their absence, disagreements shall be
referred to the Patrol Division watch commander for
resolution.
3. NOTE: Juveniles in need of medical care or under the
influence of drugs or alcohol cannot be transferred to the
custody of the Juvenile Probation Department without hospital
clearance because probation personnel will refuse such
transfers.
Page 8 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
4. If necessary, YSD shall be contacted for assistance in locating
parents of juveniles who need clearance for medical
treatment.
B. Guard Policy and Delivery of Reports
1. Unless police exigencies dictate otherwise, adult and juvenile
prisoners who need medical attention shall be accompanied
and guarded by a police officer whether the transportation is
by ambulance or police vehicle.
2. When a prisoner is not to be admitted to the hospital, the
guarding or transporting officer shall stand by while treatment
is administered.
a. If the transporting officer is a wagon officer, and if
there will be a significant delay while the prisoner
receives treatment, the member may ask the
Communications Division to dispatch a guard to relieve
him/her at the hospital.
b. The arresting officer shall be responsible for ensuring
that the arrest report or the Juvenile Record (336-606)
is completed and delivered with the prisoner to the Jail
or YSD. The arresting officer may provide
transporting and guarding officers with the information
they need to carry out these responsibilities.
3. When a prisoner is to be admitted to the hospital, the
transporting officer shall assume guard responsibilities until
relieved by Patrol Division or, in the case of juveniles, by
Probation Department personnel.
a. Wagon officers may request that Patrol Division relief
be dispatched to the hospital immediately.
b. The arresting officer shall be responsible for ensuring
that the arrest report and Declaration in Support of
Arrest (TF-2080) or the Juvenile Record are completed
Page 9 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
and delivered to the Jail or YSD without waiting for
the prisoner to be discharged from the hospital. The
arresting officer shall provide transporting and
guarding officers with the information they need to
carry out these responsibilities.
1) The Juvenile Record shall be brought directly to
YSD immediately after the juvenile is admitted
to the hospital. The third (pink) copy is left in
the juvenile's hospital record.
2) The arrest report shall be brought to the Jail as
soon as possible and the Communications
Division may be requested to dispatch the next
available wagon to deliver the report to the Jail.
c. The arresting officer shall ensure that before the arrest
report is delivered to the Jail, a member makes a
thumb print of the suspect's right and left thumb on the
back of the white and yellow copies of the
Consolidated Arrest Report so that he/she is positively
identified for booking in absentia. The member taking
prints should put his/her name and serial number next
to the prints for reporting purposes.
1) If a suspect's right or left thumb is injured or
missing, any finger may be printed, in which
case, the member shall identify on the arrest
report the finger that is used.
2) Juvenile fingerprints are not required on the
Juvenile Record. However, juvenile prints may
be taken if identity is uncertain.
C. Release of Hospital Guards - Adult Suspects
1. Pursuant to Penal Code Section 4011.7 (misdemeanor cases)
or Penal Code Section 4011.9 (felony cases) the Patrol
Page 10 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
Division watch commander may release a guard after
consulting with the Jail regarding the suspect's record.
2. Upon being released from guard duty and prior to leaving the
hospital, the guard shall complete a Request for Detention or
Police Hold form and admonish the suspect that escape from
the hospital would be a crime. These County forms are
available at the hospital.
3. The guard shall complete an Additional Information Report
(536-280), under the Report No. for the offense for which the
prisoner is in custody, to document the fact that the suspect
was admonished.
4. If the prisoner is unconscious or too sick to be admonished,
the guard shall note on the Additional Information Report that
the prisoner has not been admonished and ask the hospital
staff to telephone the Communications Division when the
prisoner regains consciousness.
5. The Communications Division shall dispatch an officer to the
hospital to admonish the prisoner and complete the required
Additional Information Report.
6. On a non-Oakland matter, i.e. out of county warrant, the
guard shall complete an Additional Information Report and
include appropriate warrant information and/or arrest
number.
7. The guard shall advise the hospital staff that the prisoner is in
the custody of the Oakland Police Department. The medical
staff is not authorized to release the prisoner.
8. The guard shall ask the hospital staff to telephone the
Communications Division when the prisoner no longer
requires medical care or attempts to leave the hospital. When
such notification is received, the Communications Division
shall ensure that arrangements are made to return the prisoner
to the Jail.
Page 11 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
D. Release of Hospital Guard - Juvenile Suspect
1. Juveniles admitted to the hospital and arrested/charged with a
serious crime(s) and likely to escape must be guarded. The
Juvenile Record shall be brought to YSD immediately so that
YSD can arrange to transfer guard responsibilities to the
Juvenile Probation Department. Until relieved by another
Patrol Division officer or by Juvenile Probation Department
personnel, the detaining officer shall assume guard
responsibilities.
2. When a juvenile prisoner, admitted to the hospital, requires a
guard, the YSD receiving officer will alert the Juvenile
Probation Department of the impending guard request. After
receiving reports from the field, the receiving officer will
immediately process them internally and then arrange for
transfer of the reports to the Juvenile Probation Department.
3. If a supervisor or command officer determines that an
arrested juvenile admitted to the hospital will not be guarded,
the officer at the scene shall notify YSD of the decision. The
appropriate reports shall be completed and forwarded to YSD
and the juvenile shall be released to a responsible adult.
V. PROPERTY OF TRANSPORTED PERSONS
A. Wagons and other transporting vehicles shall be inspected before and
after prisoner transportation to ensure that evidence and the personal
property of previously transported persons have been removed.
B. The safety of prisoners and their property and Departmental
personnel shall be given due consideration at all times. To this end,
transporting officers shall conduct a thorough search of each person
before he/she is placed in a transportation vehicle and shall take
custody of any weapons or articles which might conceivably be used
to inflict injury upon another (e.g., tools, pens, sharp objects, heavy
belt buckles, large bags and purses).
Page 12 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
C. If practicable, property taken from a person about to be transported
shall be placed in envelopes carried for that purpose in patrol
wagons, and appropriate notation of that fact shall be entered in the
Daily Patrol Wagon Transportation Log (TF-786). The name of the
prisoner shall be entered on the envelope in which his/her property
is placed.
D. Transporting officers shall be responsible for safeguarding the
property of persons in their custody until they are delivered to the
appropriate receiving agency.
E. Prisoners and their property shall be surrendered at the appropriate
receiving agency to custodial officers or as otherwise directed by
competent authority.
F. At the end of their tour of duty, wagon officers shall turn in their
Transportation Logs to the Patrol Division desk officer. The
Administrative Section of the Bureau of Field Operations shall
maintain a file of completed logs.
G. The control of property of prisoners from outside agencies shall be
handled in accordance with the provisions of Departmental General
Order H-5, PROPERTY OF PRISONERS FROM OUTSIDE
AGENCIES.
VI. FUGITIVE UNIT VEHICLES
A. The Fugitive Unit, in specially equipped vehicles assigned to the
Unit, shall arrange transportation of prisoners from other
jurisdictions where they are being held pending release to this
Department.
B. Seat belts or safety restraint devices shall be worn by all passengers
in accordance with the provisions of Departmental General Order
J-4, EMERGENCY DRIVING, PURSUIT (CODE 3), PURSUIT
INTERVENTION & SAFETY BELT REGULATIONS.
C. Fugitive Unit transport officers shall comply with the prisoner safety
and security provisions in this order.
Page 13 of 14
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
D. At the direction of the Patrol Division watch commander, prisoners
held at nearby East Bay police agencies may be transported to the
Jail or YSD in a patrol wagon or patrol car in accordance with the
provisions of this order.
E. In the event that personnel outside the Fugitive Unit need to use a
Fugitive Unit vehicle for any purpose, they shall inform the Unit as
to the reason, their destination, and the probable date and time of
return.
F. The Transportation Unit shall not release Fugitive Unit vehicles to
personnel assigned to other units without telephone clearance from
the Fugitive Unit. If Fugitive Unit personnel are unavailable,
clearance from the Patrol Division watch commander shall be
required.
By order of
Richard L. Word
Chief of Police

TRANSPORTATION OF PRISONERS AND PERSONS IN CUSTODY
The purpose of this order is to set forth Departmental policy and procedure
regarding the transportation, medical care, and guarding of prisoners and persons
in custody.
I. GENERAL TRANSPORTATION OPERATIONS AND POLICY
A. A patrol wagon shall be the standard method of transporting
prisoners and it shall contain separate compartments for males and
females. Whenever a patrol wagon is used to transport persons in
custody, the driver and the wagon officer shall sit in the front seats
separated from the prisoner(s) by a safety barrier that prevents the
prisoner(s) from having access to the driver’s compartment. Officers
shall use the seat belts when the wagon is in motion. The safety
barrier between the front and rear compartments should not impair
conversation and it should promote the safety of the occupants in the
front and/or rear compartments.

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
B. Patrol wagons shall be used to transport:
1. Adults from the point of custody to the Jail or a hospital.
2. All juveniles 12 years old and older from the point of custody
to the Youth Services Division (YSD), a hospital, or the
Juvenile Probation Department.
3. All juveniles under 12 years of age shall be transported in
standard police cars.
4. The YSD receiving officer shall be consulted before juveniles
are transported in accordance with the provisions of
Departmental General Order O-3, PROCESSING JUVENILE
OFFENDERS.
C. Prisoners shall be handcuffed in accordance with the provisions and
techniques described in Departmental Training Bulletin III-B.4,
HANDCUFFING and Special Order 4725, POSITIONAL
ASPHYXIA (20 Oct 95).
D. Use Of Marked/Caged Vehicles
1. Whenever circumstances necessitate using a standard police
patrol car to transport persons in custody, prior approval from
a supervisory officer shall be required. He/she shall specify
whether a one or two officer unit shall be assigned.
2. If two officers are in the vehicle, both officers shall sit in the
front seat.
E. Use Of Uncaged Vehicles
1. A lone officer shall avoid transporting a prisoner in a vehicle
not equipped with a cage divider. If such transportation is
imperative, the prisoner’s hands shall be handcuffed behind
his/her back and he/she is to be seated in the front passenger
seat of the vehicle with the seat belt fastened.
Page 2 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
2. When two officers are transporting one or two prisoners in a
vehicle not equipped with a cage divider, the second officer
shall sit behind the driver with the prisoner(s) seated to
his/her right, handcuffed and with the seat belt(s) fastened.
Caution shall be taken to keep the second officer’s gun side
away from the prisoner. No more than two prisoners shall be
transported in a vehicle not equipped with a cage divider.
F. The Communications Division shall be responsible for the
assignment of patrol wagons for the transport of persons in custody.
1. At the request of the Jail or YSD, the Communications
Division shall assign a wagon officer(s) to transport a
person(s) in custody from the Jail to the hospital or from YSD
to the hospital or to Juvenile Probation Department facilities,
including the facility at 150th Avenue in San Leandro.
2. Requests for use of patrol wagons beyond the scope of Part I,
F, 1 of this order (e.g., prisoner transport from other
jurisdictions) must be approved in advance by the Patrol
Division watch commander.
G. Whenever a female is transported in a standard police car, male
transporting officers shall inform the Communications Division by
radio at the beginning and at the end of the trip of both their location
and their vehicle's odometer reading.
H. Seat belts or safety restraint devices shall be worn by all occupants
in accordance with the provisions of Departmental General Order
J-4, EMERGENCY DRIVING, PURSUIT (CODE 3), PURSUIT
INTERVENTION & SAFETY BELT REGULATIONS.
I. Under no circumstances shall any vehicle with a prisoner be
involved in a pursuit or any activity that would jeopardize the safety
of the prisoner or enhance his/her chances for escape.
J. In cases where a sick, injured, or disabled prisoner is being
transported, arrangements shall be made to accommodate conditions
Page 3 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
for their transport that dictate special care and attention. The
following are examples to consider:
1. The type of vehicle to be used when transporting non-
ambulatory prisoners or those requiring wheelchairs,
crutches, or prosthetic appliances.
Prisoners in wheelchairs shall be transported directly to Santa
Rita.
2. The transfer of medicine, insulin, and other special items for
sick, injured, or disabled prisoners during transport.
3. The safety of the transporting officer and the sick, injured, or
disabled prisoner.
K. In cases where a prisoner is transported in special situations, such as
attending funerals, visiting critically ill persons, or attending the
reading of a will, arrangements shall be made in accordance with
current Jail procedures. Precautions and security measures shall be
taken in accordance with the provisions of this order.
II. TRANSPORTING OFFICERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The officer in control of the vehicle is responsible for the safety and
custody of any prisoner in his/her vehicle. A transporting officer’s
primary responsibility is the safe delivery of the prisoner(s) in their
care.
B. The transporting officer(s) shall examine the transporting vehicle
before beginning each shift to ensure that the vehicle has not been
tampered with since last used and is free of weapons and/or
evidence.
C. The transporting officer shall search every prisoner before being
transported. The search shall ensure that the prisoner is not in
possession of any weapons and/or evidence.
Page 4 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
D. Whenever the driver backs up, the passenger officer shall get out
and guide him/her.
E. An officer shall not stop to render assistance in unrelated matters.
Except in obvious and extreme circumstances, the officer shall notify
the Communications Division of the location and nature of the
incident. Under no circumstances will a prisoner in a police vehicle
be left unguarded.
F. The prisoner’s right to communicate with others, such as to an
attorney or family member, shall not be exercised during the period
that the prisoner is being transported.
G. Upon arrival at the given destination, the officer(s) transporting
prisoners to a facility must ensure that:
1. All firearms are secured and in safekeeping.
2. Restraining devices are not removed until instructed to do so
by Jail personnel in accordance with current Jail procedures.
3. All documentation regarding the transfer is delivered to the
receiving officer.
4. Prior notification is made to Jail personnel of any potential
medical or security hazards so that necessary preparations can
be made.
5. All necessary signatures from and/or written documentation
detailing the prisoner transaction are obtained from the
receiving officer.
H. Once a prisoner(s) has been transported and removed from the
vehicle, a thorough search of the transporting vehicle shall be
conducted as soon as practical, but, in all cases, before the vehicle is
reused, to ensure that the vehicle has not been tampered with since
last used, is free of weapons and/or evidence, and that all personal
property has been removed and transferred with the prisoner(s).
Page 5 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
I. In the event of an escape, the transporting officer shall immediately:
1. Notify the Communications Division and furnish the
following information:
a. That an escape has occurred
b. Description of escapee
c. Direction of flight
d. Charges
2. Notify and advise the Communications Division via telephone
to broadcast a Communications Order and notify other
agencies, if necessary.
3. Complete a supplemental report if additional charges are
added.
4. Notify a field supervisor who shall make a Patrol Log entry
and notify the Watch Commander.
J. At least one officer shall remain with the vehicle and guard the
prisoners at all times.
III. SEPARATION OF PRISONERS AND PERSONS IN CUSTODY
A. A prisoner whose attitude, condition or conduct is such as to
constitute a threat to the safety of him/herself or other persons inside
the vehicle shall be transported separately in another vehicle or, in
the case of compartmentalized wagons, in a separate section of the
wagon.
B. When being transported in compartmentalized wagons, adult
prisoners ordinarily shall be separated by sex and placed in different
sections of the vehicle. In non-compartmentalized wagons, adults
may be transported together regardless of sex.
Page 6 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
C. Juveniles shall be separated as follows:
1. Juveniles in custody for Welfare and Institutions Code Section
300 (Protective Custody) may be transported together
regardless of sex. They shall not be transported in the same
vehicle or compartment with juvenile offenders or adults.
2. Juveniles in custody for Welfare and Institutions Code
Sections 601 and 602 violations shall not be transported with
adults, nor shall they be transported with prisoners of the
opposite sex except under extraordinary circumstances or with
the permission of a supervisor. Examples of extraordinary
circumstances are as follows:
a. When a compartmentalized vehicle is unavailable and
actual or potential interference from bystanders
requires the quick removal of suspects from the arrest
scene.
b. A riot or other disturbance requires prompt
transportation of large numbers of prisoners whose
ages cannot easily be determined.
c. When extreme emergencies or priorities prevent
dispatching of more than one transporting vehicle.
D. Juvenile Disposition
1. At the request of a YSD receiving officer, the transporting
officer will stand by until a juvenile prisoner is safely
secured. When appropriate, the transporting officer will
deliver the juvenile to the Jail Division for intoxication tests
or female searches.
2. Juveniles arrested or taken into custody must be turned over
to the Juvenile Probation Department within six (6) hours
from the time they enter the police building.
Page 7 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
IV. ILL OR INJURED PERSONS

1. Adult and juvenile prisoners who need medical care shall be
transported to Highland General Hospital except in
emergency situations, in which case the closest emergency
hospital shall be utilized.
2. The Jail Division and YSD shall not accept arrested persons
for booking without medical clearance if they need medical
treatment or evaluation.

3. NOTE: Juveniles in need of medical care or under the

Page 8 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
4. If necessary, YSD shall be contacted for assistance in locating
parents of juveniles who need clearance for medical
treatment.
B. Guard Policy and Delivery of Reports

prisoners who need medical attention shall be accompanied
and guarded by a police officer whether the transportation is
by ambulance or police vehicle.
2. When a prisoner is not to be admitted to the hospital, the

is administered.

there will be a significant delay while the prisoner

b. The arresting officer shall be responsible for ensuring

Arrest (TF-2080) or the Juvenile Record are completed
Page 9 of 14

23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
and delivered to the Jail or YSD without waiting for
the prisoner to be discharged from the hospital. The
arresting officer shall provide transporting and
guarding officers with the information they need to
carry out these responsibilities.
1) The Juvenile Record shall be brought directly to
YSD immediately after the juvenile is admitted
to the hospital. The third (pink) copy is left in

2) The arrest report shall be brought to the Jail as
soon as possible and the Communications

C. Release of Hospital Guards - Adult Suspects
1. Pursuant to Penal Code Section 4011.7 (misdemeanor cases)
or Penal Code Section 4011.9 (felony cases) the Patrol

23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
Division watch commander may release a guard after
consulting with the Jail regarding the suspect's record.
2. Upon being released from guard duty and prior to leaving the
hospital, the guard shall complete a Request for Detention or

(536-280), under the Report No. for the offense for which the

was admonished.

the guard shall note on the Additional Information Report that

5. The Communications Division shall dispatch an officer to the
hospital to admonish the prisoner and complete the required

number.

shall ensure that arrangements are made to return the prisoner
to the Jail.

23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
D. Release of Hospital Guard - Juvenile Suspect
1. Juveniles admitted to the hospital and arrested/charged with a
serious crime(s) and likely to escape must be guarded. The
Juvenile Record shall be brought to YSD immediately so that

Juvenile Probation Department. Until relieved by another

guard, the YSD receiving officer will alert the Juvenile

receiving reports from the field, the receiving officer will

3. If a supervisor or command officer determines that an
arrested juvenile admitted to the hospital will not be guarded,
the officer at the scene shall notify YSD of the decision. The
appropriate reports shall be completed and forwarded to YSD
and the juvenile shall be released to a responsible adult.

B. The safety of prisoners and their property and Departmental

23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
C. If practicable, property taken from a person about to be transported
shall be placed in envelopes carried for that purpose in patrol
wagons, and appropriate notation of that fact shall be entered in the
Daily Patrol Wagon Transportation Log (TF-786). The name of the
prisoner shall be entered on the envelope in which his/her property
is placed.

E. Prisoners and their property shall be surrendered at the appropriate

Administrative Section of the Bureau of Field Operations shall
maintain a file of completed logs.
G. The control of property of prisoners from outside agencies shall be
handled in accordance with the provisions of Departmental General
Order H-5, PROPERTY OF PRISONERS FROM OUTSIDE
AGENCIES.
VI. FUGITIVE UNIT VEHICLES
A. The Fugitive Unit, in specially equipped vehicles assigned to the
Unit, shall arrange transportation of prisoners from other
jurisdictions where they are being held pending release to this
Department.
B. Seat belts or safety restraint devices shall be worn by all passengers
in accordance with the provisions of Departmental General Order
J-4, EMERGENCY DRIVING, PURSUIT (CODE 3), PURSUIT
INTERVENTION & SAFETY BELT REGULATIONS.
C. Fugitive Unit transport officers shall comply with the prisoner safety
and security provisions in this order.
Page 13 of 14

DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER O-2 Rev.
23 Mar 00OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT
D. At the direction of the Patrol Division watch commander, prisoners
held at nearby East Bay police agencies may be transported to the
Jail or YSD in a patrol wagon or patrol car in accordance with the
provisions of this order.
E. In the event that personnel outside the Fugitive Unit need to use a
Fugitive Unit vehicle for any purpose, they shall inform the Unit as
to the reason, their destination, and the probable date and time of
return.
F. The Transportation Unit shall not release Fugitive Unit vehicles to
personnel assigned to other units without telephone clearance from
the Fugitive Unit. If Fugitive Unit personnel are unavailable,
clearance from the Patrol Division watch commander shall be
required.
By order of
Richard L. Word
Chief of Police

POLICE ACTION IN CASES OF REFUSAL TO PAY FARE
The purpose of this order is to state the policy and procedures to be followed in
cases of refusal to pay fare to the driver of a taxicab as defined and provided for
in Oakland Municipal Code Section 5-29.10.
I. DEPARTMENTAL POLICY REGARDING OMC SECTION 5-29.10
A. The member concerned shall make every reasonable effort to settle
the situation without resorting to the procedures of citizen’s arrest.
B. A citizen’s arrest may be necessary:
1. When the passenger is obviously attempting to defraud the
driver.
2. When the passenger is a transient and likely to leave the area
before further legal action can be taken.
3. If the passenger has no means of identifying him/herself.
II. POLICE ACTION TO BE TAKEN
A. The criminal violation of OMC Section 5-29.10 consists of the
refusal or inability to pay the legal fare. Bona fide disputes over the
amount of fare due as recorded on a sealed meter or the inability of
the driver to make change usually are civil matters. The driver is
obligated to have enough money available to change a reasonable
amount of currency.
1. Taxicabs authorized to operate in the City of Oakland are
required to have signs affixed to the inside and outside of
DEPARTMENTAL GENERAL ORDER P-1 Rev.
OAKLAND POLICE DEPARTMENT 13 Nov 97
each vehicle which clearly state that the driver carries only
$20 in change. A $20 bill will be deemed reasonable
currency.
2. Drivers who do not have the required change are obligated to
secure the necessary change at no charge to the passenger.
B. The member shall attempt to preserve the peace by assisting the
parties in reaching a mutually satisfactory agreement.
1. The member must accept custody of the passenger if the
driver insists upon a citizen’s arrest and such arrest is valid.
Penal Code Section 142 makes it clearly mandatory for a
member to accept custody of a prisoner arrested by a citizen
who charges him/her with a criminal offense. Under these
circumstances, the member shall accept the arrestee.
2. An adult arrested shall be issued a Notice to Appear (836-
001) in the field unless the attendant circumstances establish,
in accordance with Department policy, that a physical arrest
is necessary.
3. A juvenile arrested shall be issued a Juvenile Probation
Department Notice to Appear (Form 240-40) in the field,
cited into the Juvenile Probation Department, and released.
Members shall telephone the Youth Services Division
receiving officer prior to issuing the citation in accordance
with Departmental General Order O-3, PROCESSING
JUVENILE OFFENDERS.
4. If the circumstances do not clearly indicate that a criminal
violation of OMC Section 5-29.10 has occurred and the
passenger is a bona fide resident of the area, the member shall
take a report of the incident.
By order of
Joseph Samuels, Jr.
Chief of Police GO26/P-1
